items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
COR-TRY-26-036, Investment Position as at June 30, 2026
notes:
This report was pulled from the Consent agenda by Councillor J. Gowing.

In response to questions from Committee, Lori McDonald, Manager Treasury Services & Corporate Accounting, the investment policy mainly sets limits on what the Region can and cannot do. L. McDonald also explained the priorities that staff follow under the current investment strategy which is to minimize credit risk, ensure liquidity, and maximize return on investment. Staff are currently working on a report to provide Committee with options on an updated investment strategy.

Received for information.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
COR-CFN-26-021, Reserve and Reserve Fund Sustainability
notes:
Craig Dyer, Consultant, provided a presentation. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda.

Responding to questions from Committee, C. Dyer, confirmed that the Region does still have a AAA credit rating, an updated credit rating from Moody's is anticipated to be received shortly.

C. Dyer confirmed that the numbers that make up the debt to reserve ratio would only be the Region's portion of debt outstanding and does not include any debt of lower tier municipalities.

In response to further inquires from Committee, C. Dyer explained that the Region's debt to reserve ratio has decreased down to a one to one ratio at the end of 2025. Comparing the Region's position to the other Regions in Ontario shows that the other Regions have a lower debt to reserve ratio. This means either that other Regions issue less debt than the Region of Waterloo, or that other Regions have more in their reserves and reserve funds. C. Dyer also confirmed that a significant portion of the current debt to reserve ratio is due to investments in public transit and wastewater.

C. Dyer confirmed that staff are planning on providing guidance for the next Council through orientation sessions so that the new term of Council is educated and aware of all aspects of municipal finance.  

Committee inquired into the Infrastructure funding gap. C. Dyer explained that the funding gap is cause for concern and is something that all municipalities in Ontario are currently facing. Darshpreet Bhatti, CAO, also responded on how a consolidated effort from staff and Council is needed to address the funding gap.

Committee expressed interest in receiving additional information on discretionary capital funding versus discretionary levy funding during Council orientation.

items.title: Judy Major-Girardin, Co-Chair, Cambridge Sculpture Garden
notes:
Judy Major-Girardin provided a presentation, a copy of which is attached to the agenda.

J. Major-Girardin outlined the activities of the Cambridge Sculpture Garden, and the issues around securing grant funding from municipal governments. 

In response to questions from Committee, J. Major-Girardin provided further detail on the location of the Sculpture Garden and estimates that at least 10,000 people travel through the trail that runs through the garden, especially with the re-development of the Gaslight district.

J. Major-Girardin also explained that the Sculpture Garden asked for $3,800 from the Region during the last call for grants and received $500.

items.title: Councillor P. Wolf Motion re: Drivers of Tourism Funding Allocation Criteria
notes:
Councillor P. Wolf introduced her motion to Committee. 

Committee inquired into how many grant applications from Cambridge were received in this last round; and if the more relationship building is required to ensure the Region is getting enough applications from Cambridge. Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development & Legislative Services, explained that staff have been reaching out to organizations in Cambridge to encourage applications. R. Regier also confirmed that staff are looking to bring forward a review of all grant programs and their criteria sometime in 2027. Julian Kingston, Director, Cultural services, did share that four recipients of the Cultural Drivers of Tourism Grants were from Cambridge and that staff have been working to widely advertise grant opportunities.

Committee inquired into the Municipal Accommodation Tax (MAT) and how it is distributed. J. Kingston shared that the MAT is divided between the Region with 10%, the area municipality with 50%, and Explore Waterloo Region with 40%. 

Additional discussion occurred around how the current MAT allocation formula was developed and how the proper allocation gets distributed to each municipality.

motions.item_title: Councillor P. Wolf Motion re: Drivers of Tourism Funding Allocation Criteria
motions.text: WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo's Cultural Drivers of Tourism program provides funding from the Municipal Accommodation Tax (MAT) Reserve to support arts, cultural, and heritage organizations that attract visitors to Waterloo Region; and WHEREAS hotels located throughout Waterloo Region generate the Municipal Accommodation Tax revenues that fund this program; and WHEREAS the 2026 funding allocations resulted in Cambridge-based organizations receiving approximately $3,000 of the $250,000 available through the program, despite Cambridge being home to a significant number of accommodation providers contributing to the MAT Reserve; WHEREAS a sustainable cultural tourism strategy should recognize both visitor attraction outcomes and the contribution of municipalities that generate the revenues supporting the program; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to review the Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding formula and eligibility criteria to determine whether amendments are warranted to ensure a more equitable geographic distribution of funding across the Region's municipalities; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the review include consideration of: 1. The relationship between Municipal Accommodation Tax revenue generation and funding allocations; 2. Mechanisms to ensure all municipalities receive fair consideration under the program; 3. The long-term impact of current allocation practices on cultural development and tourism growth in municipalities receiving minimal funding; and 4. Alternative funding models that balance visitor attraction metrics with regional equity objectives. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff report back to Council with recommendations prior to the next Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding intake.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo's Cultural Drivers of Tourism program provides funding from the Municipal Accommodation Tax (MAT) Reserve to support arts, cultural, and heritage organizations that attract visitors to Waterloo Region; and

WHEREAS hotels located throughout Waterloo Region generate the Municipal Accommodation Tax revenues that fund this program; and

WHEREAS the 2026 funding allocations resulted in Cambridge-based organizations receiving approximately $3,000 of the $250,000 available through the program, despite Cambridge being home to a significant number of accommodation providers contributing to the MAT Reserve;

WHEREAS a sustainable cultural tourism strategy should recognize both visitor attraction outcomes and the contribution of municipalities that generate the revenues supporting the program;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to review the Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding formula and eligibility criteria to determine whether amendments are warranted to ensure a more equitable geographic distribution of funding across the Region's municipalities; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the review include consideration of:

1. The relationship between Municipal Accommodation Tax revenue generation and funding allocations;

2. Mechanisms to ensure all municipalities receive fair consideration under the program;

3. The long-term impact of current allocation practices on cultural development and tourism growth in municipalities receiving minimal funding; and

4. Alternative funding models that balance visitor attraction metrics with regional equity objectives.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff report back to Council with recommendations prior to the next Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding intake.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. James Motion re: Stanley Park Community Association Mural Project
motions.text: WHEREAS the late Kari Williams served the residents of Waterloo Region with dedication, compassion, and a strong commitment to community well-being; and WHEREAS Kari Williams was a passionate supporter of the Stanley Park Eats program, which provides meals and support to community members in need; and WHEREAS the Stanley Park Community Association is leading a community mural project on the Stanley Park Eats serving hut; and WHEREAS the mural has been inspired by Kari Williams' commitment to addressing food insecurity and supporting the Stanley Park community; and WHEREAS the project has received funding through a $6,500 LoveMyHood grant from the City of Kitchener and contributions from the Stanley Park Community Association, and community fundraising efforts; and WHEREAS community art projects help create vibrant public spaces and strengthen neighbourhood pride; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Regional Council approve a one-time grant of $2,000 from the Municipal Accommodation Tax Reserve Public Art Reserve Fund to the Stanley Park Community Association to support the Stanley Park Eats mural project; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Regional Council recognizes the lasting contributions of Kari Williams to the Stanley Park community and Waterloo Region; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Corporate Services be authorized to take all necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS the late Kari Williams served the residents of Waterloo Region with dedication, compassion, and a strong commitment to community well-being; and

WHEREAS Kari Williams was a passionate supporter of the Stanley Park Eats program, which provides meals and support to community members in need; and

WHEREAS the Stanley Park Community Association is leading a community mural project on the Stanley Park Eats serving hut; and

WHEREAS the mural has been inspired by Kari Williams' commitment to addressing food insecurity and supporting the Stanley Park community; and

WHEREAS the project has received funding through a $6,500 LoveMyHood grant from the City of Kitchener and contributions from the Stanley Park Community Association, and community fundraising efforts; and

WHEREAS community art projects help create vibrant public spaces and strengthen neighbourhood pride;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Regional Council approve a one-time grant of $2,000 from the Municipal Accommodation Tax Reserve Public Art Reserve Fund to the Stanley Park Community Association to support the Stanley Park Eats mural project; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Regional Council recognizes the lasting contributions of Kari Williams to the Stanley Park community and Waterloo Region; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Corporate Services be authorized to take all necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution.
